text:
Josh Norris arrived in Buffalo from Ottawa with a reputation as a goal scorer and a long history of shoulder trouble. He played 44 games last season. This year he's healthy, and the points haven't come: seven in 21 games, on 14:13 a night.

Our numbers say be patient. The Sabres have scored 9.9 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on the ice, one of the bigger gaps in the league, and that kind of luck usually turns. Meanwhile the process is solid: Buffalo takes 53% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him out there, nearly four points better than without him. His own shooting isn't the problem; four goals on 4.35 expected is right on.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.4 wins last season, 110th among forwards, mostly from even-strength offense. A player with 104 goals before turning 27 doesn't usually stay at a third-line scoring pace for long when the underlying numbers look like this. The thing to watch is his ice time, down to 13:29 over the last ten games. If the bounces come, the minutes should too.
headline: Norris is driving play without the points
